pages.text: From erectus, a $(l)log$() in your hand and a $(l)hide$() in the other, then $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact): the log stood on end, the hide lashed over the top of it. Somewhere to work more than stone.

A grid, and a tool slot beside it. Nothing comes of the grid without the right thing in that slot - the tool is what the recipe actually is.$(br2)A hand axe against a log, or a long branch, makes a $(l)workable branch$(). Two of them down the middle with a hammerstone make a $(l)club$().

One workable branch with a $(l)cleaver$() in the slot is trued end to end into a $(l)workable shaft$(): straight and even, the stock stone spears, proper digging sticks and hunting spears will be made on.$(br2)In the hand, worked wood is still a long branch - same reach, same swing - but it wears, and a worn-out one is just a long branch again.

A branch with any $(l)three rocks$() - one kind or a mix, anywhere in the grid - makes two $(l)building branches$(): the posts a hut or a tent stands on. A branch with $(l)three sticks$() makes a $(l)cooking rack$() (see The Cooking Rack).$(br2)Ten twine, a branch and a hammerstone side by side make a proper $(l)digging stick$().

A grid of $(l)thatch$(), four twine in the tool slot, makes a thatch block. Left as it is, the weather takes it apart - stretch hide over it and it stops caring.$(br2)Three hide over a row of thatch, ten twine in the slot, makes two pieces of $(l)bedding$(). Lay them side by side to sleep in - a real bed, and unlike a nest it does not leave you with ticks.

Three logs along the bottom row, sticks in the rest but the top middle, nothing in the slot: a $(l)fire pit$() (see Keeping Fire).$(br2)Thatch over a stick - thatch in the top middle, the stick under it - with three twine in the slot: a $(l)torch$().$(br2)Planks are not a thing anyone here would make: wood is split, not sawn.
